notes: Source-verified, same functional-gating pattern as chatwoot.json and zammad.json. requirements/base.txt pins openai==1.63.2. plane/app/views/external/base.py implements an LLMProvider abstraction (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini classes; model lists include gpt-4o, claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620, gemini-pro) via get_llm_config()/get_llm_response() calling OpenAI(api_key=...).chat.completions.create(...). Two real endpoints confirmed in plane/app/urls/external.py: POST /workspaces/<slug>/projects/<project_id>/ai-assistant/ -> GPTIntegrationEndpoint, POST /workspaces/<slug>/ai-assistant/ -> WorkspaceGPTIntegrationEndpoint. AUTH VERIFIED (not just assumed): both endpoints decorated with @allow_permission([ROLE.ADMIN, ROLE.MEMBER]) (base.py:149,185), and their common parent BaseAPIView sets permission_classes=[IsAuthenticated] and authentication_classes=[BaseSessionAuthentication] (views/base.py:150,154) — real session-based auth is required before the role check even runs. FUNCTIONAL CAVEAT (why 'partial' not 'yes'): both view methods start with `api_key, model, provider = get_llm_config()` then `if not api_key or not model or not provider:` — same admin-must-configure-a-provider-key gating pattern as Chatwoot's Captain and Zammad's AI assistance; live and auth-gated, but inert until an admin supplies LLM credentials, which was not verified as present in this container.

must_not_report.reason: Both GPT integration endpoints require IsAuthenticated + role-based allow_permission — no unauthenticated path exists
